items.item_text: Bachelor’s Degree in Biology or related field with an emphasis in infectious disease or 5-7 years of experience or/and equivalent combination of education and experience.
Masters degree, with field of study or emphasis in epidemiology and biostatistics, or 3-5 years of experience preferred,

Experience communicating effectively and professionally and working with a variety of internal and external partners, including UCLA administrators, outside funders, policy makers and community representatives.
Training and > 3 years experience in LDMS (Laboratory and Data Management System) by Frontier Science
Intermediate knowledge/experience in R software
Intermediate knowledge/experience in Redcap

The Department is seeking an experienced Program/Project Manager to lead the planning, development, and execution of program/project operations in a fast-paced environment. The incumbent will coordinate research and program activities, oversee deliverables and budgets, support grant development, lead meetings and strategic planning, and supervise staff while ensuring compliance with UCLA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Plan, develop, and execute program/project operations to achieve established goals and objectives.
Coordinate IRB protocol submissions and approvals and ensure compliance with UCLA, federal, and state regulations.
Manage day-to-day program and research activities, including outreach and recruitment, participant consent, surveys/interviews, status reporting, and project documentation.
Develop schedules, workflow timelines, databases, and other materials needed to support program/project operations.
Participate in data collection, data cleaning, analysis, and literature reviews.
Lead the development and production of program/project deliverables, including reports, presentations, websites, social media content, communications, and related materials.
Plan and manage program/project budgets in accordance with UCLA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Lead grant writing activities and coordinate proposal submissions.
Plan and coordinate internal and external meetings, conferences, site visits, and related events, including agendas, meeting materials, speakers, and follow-up activities.
Evaluate program/project data and operations to identify areas for improvement and develop strategic plans, solutions, and best practices.
Represent the program/project effectively with leadership, stakeholders, community partners, and the public through appropriate communication channels, including social media and online platforms.
Supervise and lead program/project teams, anticipate staffing needs, and provide oversight to ensure effective and efficient operations.
Train and develop new and existing staff
Ability to work independently and also have interpersonal skills to work with teams, provide training, and supervise staff.
Exceptional writing skills to produce wide range of documents and deliverables.

Strong organizational skills to successfully work on and track complex programs involving short deadlines and multiple tasks, in coordination with multiple teams to achieve program/project mission and goals.

Working knowledge of program/project development, evaluation, creating datasets, financial management and reporting, research principles including CITI training, grant writing and proposal submission, University procedures and policies, program/project related federal and state regulations.
Ability to seek out and learn new policies, procedures, and software to advance the mission of the program/project.
Ability to train new program/project managers and other staff within and external to the unit.
Demonstrated ability to communicate medical, policy and administrative information.
